title: Do Generate–Verify–Repair Guards Improve LLM NetOps Outputs? A Paired Emulator Study
abstract: We preregistered and executed a paired confirmatory experiment (n=200 natural-language NetOps intents; study_id cnd-001-5f3a) that compares ungated LLM generation to a bounded generate–verify–repair (GVR) pipeline applied to a single shared LLM candidate per intent. Generation used gpt-5-mini and the guarded arm applied a deterministic three-stage validator and a deterministic, rule-based repair operator with repair_budget ≤1 (no extra LLM calls). Artifact-backed primary outcomes: baseline successes = 199/200 (0.995), guarded = 200/200 (1.000); paired contingency n11=199, n10=1, n01=0, n00=0; paired difference (guarded − baseline) = 0.005. The preregistered exact two-sided McNemar (exact binomial on discordant pairs) yields p = 1.0; paired-bootstrap (10,000 resamples, seed 1729) 95% percentile CI = [0.0, 0.015]. The preregistered 0.15 absolute-effect target is excluded by the observed CI because the realized baseline was near-ceiling. We report concise, auditable descriptions of the validator and repair operator, execution accounting (model_calls_used = 201; deterministic repair invocations = 1), exact-test justification appropriate for small discordant counts, and operationally grounded limitations. All prompts, provider traces, validator traces, repair traces (the single invoked repair trace), and analysis artifacts are archived in the study evidence bundle (see Disclosure).

sections.introduction:
Automating routine network-operations (NetOps) changes with large language models (LLMs) promises reduced manual effort but raises an operational-safety question: do LLM-produced configuration artifacts execute correctly when applied to control planes? Prior work demonstrates intent-to-configuration prototypes and documents structured-output failures (missing commands, misordering, protected-field modification) and proposes mitigations such as retrieval-augmentation, constrained decoding, verifier-assisted repair, and multi-stage tool-augmentation. Despite these proposals, there is limited execution-grounded evidence that quantifies the marginal benefit of applying a bounded deterministic repair to the same initial LLM candidate (a low-hosted-call operational estimand).

We preregistered and executed a paired experiment (study_id cnd-001-5f3a) that isolates the “repair-on-same-candidate” question by sharing a single initial LLM candidate across both arms (baseline ungated acceptance and guarded generate–verify–repair). The shared-candidate estimand is operationally relevant when hosted-model call budgets are constrained. Our contributions are: (1) a preregistered, artifact-backed paired evaluation under the shared-candidate estimand; (2) concise algorithmic descriptions of the deterministic three-stage validator and the deterministic, rule-based repair operator used in the guarded pipeline; and (3) complete execution accounting and exact-test justification for small-discordant-pair inference.
sections.related_work:
Three strands of prior work inform this study. First, intent-to-configuration research shows LLMs can synthesize CLI-like commands but that structured-output errors are common without additional constraints; representative empirical intent-translation work documents prototype success under curated conditions and highlights missing-required-commands, ordering errors, and protected-field violations (Nguyen et al., 2024) [doi:10.1002/nem.2313]. Second, mitigation approaches from adjacent domains—retrieval-augmented generation (RAG), schema grounding, and constrained decoding—reduce hallucinations and format errors in NL2SQL, document grounding, and other structured-output tasks (Geng et al., 2023). Third, deterministic formal verifiers and emulator-based validators (NetKAT variants, ensemble verifiers, emulator checks) provide natural assurance layers for generated configurations, though they do not fully capture dynamic control-plane timing or vendor idiosyncrasies (Suárez Acevedo et al., 2026) [doi:10.1145/3808318].

Generate–verify–repair (GVR) architectures combining generation, deterministic checking, and repair are repeatedly proposed, but fully instrumented, execution-grounded, preregistered paired evaluations that isolate same-candidate repairs under constrained model-call budgets remain scarce. This study directly targets that gap (candidate gap G2 in our evidence synthesis).
sections.methodology:
Preregistration and design: We preregistered a paired, shared-initial-generation confirmatory protocol (study_id cnd-001-5f3a). For each of n = 200 curated natural-language intents the hosted model produced one initial candidate which served both as the baseline output and as the input to the guarded pipeline. The guarded arm invoked a deterministic three-stage validator; when the validator reported a repairable violation the pipeline ran a deterministic, rule-based repair operator (repair_budget ≤ 1; no additional LLM calls). The primary estimand is the paired success-rate difference (guarded − baseline); the preregistered primary test is the exact two-sided McNemar (exact binomial on discordant pairs). Planned maximum hosted-model calls = 400; realized model_calls_used = 201 (shared_initial_generation = 200; deterministic repair-stage calls = 1). The execution environment combined Dockerized Mininet+FRR with deterministic_netops_validator_v5 as the canonical validator.

Task bank and scoring: The confirmatory bank contains 200 intent–expected-configuration pairs generated deterministically; each task payload contains initial_state, expected_final_state, required_sequence (authoritative ordered steps), workflow_policies (e.g., make-before-break, minimum-active constraints), and difficulty metadata. Scoring (full_intent_constraint_validation) requires (a) syntactic parse, (b) presence and canonical order of required_sequence commands, (c) satisfaction of dependency and group-activity policies, (d) preservation of protected-interface values, and (e) emulator-observed final_state equality with expected_final_state. Provider/API generation failures are treated per the preregistered missingness plan as arm failures; none occurred in the confirmatory run.

Deterministic validator and repair operator: The validator deterministically performs three ordered stages: Stage 1 — syntactic parsing and canonical normalization into a normalized_configuration; Stage 2 — structural and workflow checks emitting deterministic violation codes (e.g., MISSING_REQUIRED_COMMAND, DEPENDENCY_VIOLATION, PROTECTED_INTERFACE_MODIFICATION, TRANSIENT_ORDER_VIOLATION); Stage 3 — deterministic emulator application to produce observed final_state and a final boolean valid indicator. The repair operator is a manifest-driven deterministic transformer invoked only for violation families in a preregistered repairable set and only when the mapping from violation code to deterministic transformation is unique. Repairs are implemented without further LLM calls and consist of canonical transformations (insertion, reordering, or preservation enforcement) derived from task.required_sequence, initial_state, expected_final_state and workflow_policies. Ambiguous or multiply-plausible cases cause abstention (no edit) and are recorded as nonrepairable. Repair decisions and resulting normalized_configuration are archived per episode.
sections.results:
Execution and primary outcomes: The confirmatory run completed all planned episodes (400 episodes = 200 paired intents) with no provider/API failures. Condition-level counts (artifact-backed) show baseline_successes = 199/200 (0.995) and guarded_successes = 200/200 (1.000). The paired contingency is n11 = 199, n10 = 1, n01 = 0, n00 = 0; paired difference (guarded − baseline) = 0.005.

Exact-test and CI: The preregistered exact two-sided McNemar (exact binomial on discordant pairs) computed on n = 1 discordant pair gives two-sided p = 1.0 (analysis executor). Complementary uncertainty quantification used a paired-bootstrap percentile 95% CI with 10,000 resamples (bootstrap_seed = 1729) yielding 95% CI = [0.0, 0.015]. The preregistered target absolute effect (0.15) is excluded by the observed CI because the baseline was near-ceiling. The analysis artifacts (analysis/paired_contingency_table.csv and analysis/condition_summary.csv) and the bootstrap parameters are archived.

Single repaired episode: The validator reported validation_before.valid == false in exactly one confirmatory episode; deterministic repair invocations = 1 and that single deterministic repair converted the episode into a validator-passing configuration, producing the sole guarded-only success (n10 = 1). The full per-episode records that contain the episode identifier, validator.violation_codes, the deterministic repair_trace (transformation name, before/after normalized_configuration), and other audit fields are archived in the execution/raw_results.jsonl (SHA-256: e3bb0089bb742517e662dd434db4a44e2f0f6b5f1da8b3151a309a7a6d5a3a58) and in the execution/task_manifest.jsonl (SHA-256: eb2f045f8a6214eb6d814e16f5d95e0120bd89973951b6fe14084bda4e3efb4a). Readers can inspect those artifacts to obtain the task identifier, exact violation codes, the canonical deterministic repair(s) applied, and the before/after normalized_configuration snippets; the repair_trace fields include canonical transformation names (insertion/reordering/preservation enforcement) and the normalized text before and after the deterministic operator.

Difficulty-distribution summary (artifact reference): The confirmatory bank carries per-task difficulty labels (very_hard, hard, medium, easy) produced by the deterministic task generator. The full 200-entry distribution of these labels is recorded in execution/task_manifest.jsonl (SHA-256: eb2f045f8a6214eb6d814e16f5d95e0120bd89973951b6fe14084bda4e3efb4a). To preserve concise presentation while keeping the study auditable, we reference that manifest for exact counts; the manifest contains the complete per-task difficulty field for every confirmatory intent and can be programmatically aggregated by readers wishing to reproduce the distribution counts.
sections.discussion:
Operational interpretation: Under the shared-initial-generation estimand and this curated confirmatory distribution, ungated gpt-5-mini generation produced near-perfect candidates (199/200). Deterministic, auditable validators produce structured violation codes enabling targeted deterministic repairs; in this low-error regime the marginal yield of a conservative rule-based repair on the same candidate is small but auditable and low-cost. For operators constrained by model-call budgets, a shared-candidate guarded design preserves low hosted-call cost while providing an assurance gate; for contexts prioritizing maximal pass rates, independent-resampling or LLM-guided iterative repair would likely increase yield at higher provider cost.

Formal sensitivity note (preregistered power vs. observed baseline): Our preregistered power analysis targeted a 0.15 absolute improvement assuming baseline ≈ 0.5 and n = 200 pairs. The observed baseline (0.995) collapses discordant-pair opportunities (observed discordants n = n10 + n01 = 1), substantially reducing power to detect large preregistered effects under the shared-candidate estimand. Concretely, with only one discordant pair the exact McNemar two-sided test is uninformative for large effect sizes; the paired-bootstrap CI [0.0, 0.015] quantifies the achievable precision under the realized data. This post-hoc mismatch—baseline assumption versus realized baseline—limits the confirmatory inference and explains why the preregistered 0.15 effect is not supported.

Threats to validity and operational implications: Internal validity is strong for the paired estimand and deterministic scoring; construct validity depends on emulator fidelity—the deterministic emulator models control-plane state deterministically but cannot capture runtime dynamics such as BGP convergence timing or vendor firmware idiosyncrasies. External validity is limited by the single LLM (gpt-5-mini) and the synthetic curated bank; extrapolation to multivendor CLI diversity or adversarial intents is limited. Conclusion validity is constrained by the near-ceiling baseline and the small number of discordants. Practically, deterministic validators are valuable audit gates and diagnostic machinery; their marginal yield under low-error generators is small but still operationally useful because they provide auditable failure diagnostics and enable targeted low-cost deterministic repairs when the mapping is unambiguous.

Reproducibility and auditability: All artifacts needed to reproduce analysis and inspect the single repaired episode are archived. Key artifact references: execution/raw_results.jsonl (SHA-256: e3bb0089bb742517e662dd434db4a44e2f0f6b5f1da8b3151a309a7a6d5a3a58), execution/task_manifest.jsonl (SHA-256: eb2f045f8a6214eb6d814e16f5d95e0120bd89973951b6fe14084bda4e3efb4a), execution/model_configuration.json (SHA-256: a40e96e212ab87da251ac0d6dbb75bc543afa13438b5a6b9ebd073597ffdd820). The repair_trace, validator_trace, and provider-call traces are all present in the evidence bundle for per-episode forensic inspection. Future work should evaluate independent-resampling estimands, larger multivendor banks, and adversarial-intent stress tests to quantify repair yield under higher baseline-error regimes.
sections.conclusion: We executed an autonomy-locked, preregistered paired experiment to measure whether a bounded generate–verify–repair guard improves emulator-executable success for LLM-generated NetOps configurations under a shared-candidate generation budget. Ungated gpt-5-mini generation succeeded in 199/200 confirmatory cases; the deterministic guarded pipeline succeeded in 200/200. The observed paired difference = 0.005 (exact McNemar two-sided p = 1.0; paired-bootstrap 95% CI [0.0, 0.015]) does not support the preregistered 0.15 absolute-effect target because the baseline was near-ceiling. Deterministic validators remain valuable, auditable assurance gates for operational NetOps pipelines; low-cost deterministic repairs on the same shared candidate produced one auditable conversion in this confirmatory bank. All artifacts and analysis code are archived for independent audit and re-analysis.

disclosure_statement:
This study was executed autonomously after an autonomy lock defined by the initial master prompt archived at provenance/master_prompt.txt (SHA-256: 1872df1e1805d2d96940456ca016bd665d1d5196add77f5acdf1582bb39b15ba). Human involvement prior to the lock was limited to selecting the topic family (Generative AI and LLMs for NetOps) and approving the master prompt. No manual human editing of technical content, figures, captions, references, results, or manuscript text occurred after the lock. The autonomous pipeline performed literature search and verification, research-gap selection, preregistration (study_id cnd-001-5f3a), code generation, experiment execution, artifact capture, analysis, internal critique, peer-review checks, and manuscript drafting.

Models and tooling: generation requested gpt-5-mini (declared_model_version in execution/model_configuration.json; execution/model_configuration.json SHA-256: a40e96e212ab87da251ac0d6dbb75bc543afa13438b5a6b9ebd073597ffdd820). Validation used deterministic_netops_validator_v5 implementing syntactic parsing, structural/workflow checks, and deterministic emulator application. Repairs in the confirmatory run were applied by deterministic code only (no additional LLM calls). The execution environment used Dockerized Mininet+FRR images orchestrated by adapter family hosted_netops_gvr_v1. Preregistered and enforced settings (not altered post-lock) include: primary estimand = paired_success_rate_difference_guarded_minus_baseline; confirmatory sample = n=200 paired intents; maximum model-call budget = 400; repair budget ≤1 deterministic repair iteration; primary analysis = exact McNemar two-sided (exact-binomial on discordant pairs); bootstrap CIs = 10,000 resamples, seed = 1729. Execution accounting (artifact-backed) shows the run completed 400 episodes with model_calls_used = 201 (shared_initial_generation = 200; repair-stage calls = 1). All prompts, provider-call traces, responses, validator traces, repair traces (the single invoked repair trace), analysis artifacts, and the execution manifest are archived in the study evidence bundle. Key artifact entry points for audit: execution/raw_results.jsonl (SHA-256: e3bb0089bb742517e662dd434db4a44e2f0f6b5f1da8b3151a309a7a6d5a3a58) and execution/task_manifest.jsonl (SHA-256: eb2f045f8a6214eb6d814e16f5d95e0120bd89973951b6fe14084bda4e3efb4a).
limitations: Synthetic, curated confirmatory task bank focused on small single- and small multi-device changes; not comprehensive of production NetOps workloads (multivendor CLI dialects, hardware idiosyncrasies, dynamic control-plane timing).
Single LLM (gpt-5-mini) evaluated; findings do not imply multi-model generality.
Deterministic emulator + validator model control-plane behavior but cannot fully capture real-world runtime dynamics such as BGP convergence timing or vendor-specific runtime effects.
Preregistered repair budget limited to a single deterministic repair iteration; different repair strategies or additional iterations might yield different outcomes.
Shared-initial-generation design reduces model-call cost and isolates repair-on-same-candidate effectiveness but reduces external generalizability compared with independent-resampling estimands.
Near-ceiling baseline success limited statistical power to analyze failure-mode distributions in the confirmatory set; exploratory failure-taxonomy conclusions are therefore constrained.
Adversarial or out-of-distribution intents (e.g., jailbreaks, malformed ambiguous intents) were not included in the confirmatory set and require separate evaluation.

The full per-task difficulty label distribution for the 200 confirmatory intents is recorded in execution/task_manifest.jsonl (SHA-256: eb2f045f8a6214eb6d814e16f5d95e0120bd89973951b6fe14084bda4e3efb4a) and is referenced here to preserve concise presentation while enabling auditable reproduction.
